speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your baby's condition, could you describe the specific nature of his feeding difficulties and whether he has experienced any vomiting or diarrhea? Also, when did you first notice the abdominal distension?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby have a fever, and is he passing stool regularly, or is he constipated? Also, has he had any recent injuries or trauma to the abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the baby passing any stool, and if so, what does it look like (e.g., color, consistency)? Also, has he had a bowel movement since birth, or was there any significant delay in passing meconium?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass any stool at all now, and if so, is it small, pellet-like, or explosive? Also, has a barium enema or abdominal X-ray been performed to check for a transition zone?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.
